key_insight: TACO is a memory-efficient optimizer designed to keep AdamW-like fine-tuning behavior while drastically reducing optimizer state overhead. It targets the main bottleneck in full-parameter LLM fine-tuning: fitting large models and their optimizer states on limited GPU memory.
problem_solved: Full-parameter fine-tuning of large language models requires storing large optimizer states, which consumes a lot of GPU memory and limits the largest models that can be trained. Existing memory-saving optimizers often change the update geometry or reduce performance compared with AdamW.
method: Uses a ternary, absolute-max, column-wise, one-sparse update scheme to compress optimizer state.
Aims to preserve AdamW-like optimization behavior while reducing memory footprint.
Provides an alternative to dense-state optimizers and geometry-changing methods such as matrix-valued updates.
impact: This approach can enable fine-tuning larger LLMs on the same hardware budget, making advanced adaptation more accessible to researchers and practitioners. It is especially relevant when preserving AdamW-style performance is important but GPU memory is tight.
